entries.name: Mire Hag
entries.text: A swamp witch who lures travelers with lantern light, then drags them under the black water. She bargains, but always takes more than she gives.

entries.name: Gloomfang
entries.text: A cave wolf the size of a pony, grey as ash, with one milky eye. Hunts in the hills above the village at dusk.

entries.name: Ash Wyrm
entries.text: An old dragon asleep under the burnt mountain. Its breath is smoke and cinders; the slopes are warm to the touch.

entries.name: Brother Aldric
entries.text: The village priest. Kind, tired, and secretly paying the Mire Hag in silver so she spares the village children.

entries.name: Sela Venn
entries.text: The blacksmith. Broad-shouldered, quick to laugh, forges the only steel in the valley. Lost her brother to the wolf.

entries.name: The Drowned Bell
entries.text: A bronze bell sunk in the marsh. When it rings underwater, someone in the village dies before morning.

entries.name: Hollowmere
entries.text: A small village of thatched houses between the hills and the marsh. One inn, one chapel, one forge.

entries.name: The Salt Road
entries.text: The old trade road out of the valley, lined with mile-stones carved with warding runes. Merchants avoid it after dark.

entries.name: Ironwood Staff
entries.text: A walking staff of black wood that never burns. Whoever carries it cannot be lied to.

entries.name: The Crooked Inn
entries.text: Hollowmere's only inn, run by a nervous widower. The ale is thin, the beds are clean, and the cellar door is always locked.

entries.name: Grave Lanterns
entries.text: Little blue lights that drift over the graveyard. Following them leads to the dead, not the living.

entries.name: Captain Roderick Vale
entries.text: Leader of the valley's small militia. Gruff, honest, badly outnumbered, and drinking too much since the wyrm stirred.

entries.name: The Black Fen
entries.text: The deepest part of the marsh, where the water is black and still and the reeds grow taller than a man.

entries.name: Moonpetal
entries.text: A pale flower that only opens at night. Brewed into tea, it cures fever; eaten raw, it brings visions.

entries.name: The Ember Cult
entries.text: Robed worshippers of the Ash Wyrm who want to wake it. They mark their doors with a burnt handprint.

scenes.scene: I ask the witch what she wants in return.
Something with long fingers rises out of the bog and smiles at me.
A huge grey beast with one pale eye watches us from the ridge.
We hear howling from the hills as the sun goes down.
The ground on the mountain is warm and smoke leaks from the cracks.
I tell the captain the dragon is waking.
I confront the priest about the silver missing from the chapel.
I need a sword forged before the attack.
I ask Sela if she can fix my armor.
Far out in the marsh, something bronze tolls beneath the water.
We reach the village at last: a handful of thatched roofs and a chapel.
We take the old trade route out of the valley before nightfall.
I lean on the black walking stick and ask him to tell me the truth.
I want a room and a drink for the night.
Why is the cellar door locked?
Small blue lights float above the tombstones and drift away.
The militia leader is drunk again.
We wade into the deepest, darkest part of the swamp where the reeds tower over us.
The child has a terrible fever. Is there any remedy?
Someone has pressed a burnt handprint onto the door of the inn.
